item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"medium","summary":"B is preferable for its stronger retry verification, clearer validation errors, and useful user-facing documentation, though neither patch is merge-ready because both bypass FilesService.Add in direct violation of the contract.","reasons":["Both patches duplicate Add's option handling, Raw.Do call, response decoding, and missing-data error instead of routing the multipart body through s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), creating the exact maintenance divergence the contract forbids.","B's retry test parses the multipart body on every attempt and verifies that the file content survives the 429 replay; A only verifies the number of calls, so it could miss an empty or corrupted replayed body.","B reports empty filename and nil content separately, while A returns the misleading combined message \"file name and content are required\" when only one argument is invalid.","B's README example directly addresses the reported os.Open workflow and clearly distinguishes Upload from the lower-level Add API."],"risks_a":["No tests cover empty-filename validation, nil-content validation, or source-reader failures.","The retry test does not inspect either attempted request body, weakening verification of the core replay requirement.","The changelog is unusually implementation-specific and exposes internal helper and net/http details."],"risks_b":["No tests cover empty-filename validation, nil-content validation, or source-reader failures.","The retry test uses strings.NewReader rather than a deliberately non-replayable or streaming source, despite checking replayed request content well.","The additional Add limitation test and documentation modestly broaden the patch, though they remain relevant to the reported behavior."]}
